rows.text: |  Feature  |  AWS Fargate  |  AWS Lambda  |

cells.col3: AWS Lambda

rows.text: |  Execution model  |  Container-based, serverless compute  |  Event-driven, serverless functions (with optional durable orchestration)  |

cells.col3: Event-driven, serverless functions (with optional durable orchestration)

rows.text: |  Supported languages  |  Any language that can run in a container  |  Node.js, Python, Java, C\#, Go, Ruby, and PowerShell. You can also [build a custom runtime](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-custom.html) for other languages. |

cells.col2: Any language that can run in a container
cells.col3: Node.js, Python, Java, C\#, Go, Ruby, and PowerShell. You can also [build a custom runtime](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-custom.html) for other languages.

rows.text: |  Use case  |  Long-running, containerized applications  |  Short-duration, event-driven tasks (or workflows up to 1 year with durable functions)  |

cells.col3: Short-duration, event-driven tasks (or workflows up to 1 year with durable functions)

rows.text: |  Execution pattern  |  Continuous compute (long-running processes, persistent connections)  |  Event-driven with optional wait-heavy orchestration (durable functions)  |

cells.col3: Event-driven with optional wait-heavy orchestration (durable functions)

rows.text: |  Scaling  |  Automatic scaling based on desired task count, with predictive scaling support  |  Automatic scaling per request  |

cells.col2: Automatic scaling based on desired task count, with predictive scaling support
cells.col3: Automatic scaling per request

rows.text: |  Cold start  |  Varies by image size and configuration  |  Varies by runtime and package size  |

cells.col2: Varies by image size and configuration
cells.col3: Varies by runtime and package size

rows.text: |  Execution time limit  |  No hard limit  |  15 minutes per invocation (durable functions orchestrate workflows up to 1 year)  |

cells.col3: 15 minutes per invocation (durable functions orchestrate workflows up to 1 year)

rows.text: |  Memory allocation  |  Up to 244 GiB  |  Up to 10 GiB  |

cells.col3: Up to 10 GiB

rows.text: |  CPU allocation  |  Up to 32 vCPU  |  Proportional to memory, up to 6 vCPU  |

cells.col3: Proportional to memory, up to 6 vCPU

rows.text: |  Networking  |  Runs in VPC with ENIs; supports Amazon VPC Lattice and IPv6-only configurations  |  Can run in AWS managed VPC or attached to a customer-managed VPC using AWS Hyperplane |

cells.col2: Runs in VPC with ENIs; supports Amazon VPC Lattice and IPv6-only configurations
cells.col3: Can run in AWS managed VPC or attached to a customer-managed VPC using AWS Hyperplane

rows.text: |  State management  |  Containers can maintain in-memory state across requests while running. External storage is recommended for critical data.  |  Stateless by design (state must be managed externally, for example, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EFS). Durable functions can persist workflow state for up to 1 year.  |

cells.col2: Containers can maintain in-memory state across requests while running. External storage is recommended for critical data.
cells.col3: Stateless by design (state must be managed externally, for example, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EFS). Durable functions can persist workflow state for up to 1 year.

rows.text: |  Container support  |  Full container support  |  Limited container support (via container image deployments)  |

cells.col3: Limited container support (via container image deployments)

rows.text: |  Orchestration  |  Integrated with Amazon ECS |  No orchestration required  |

cells.col3: No orchestration required

rows.text: |  Deployment strategies  |  Native blue/green, canary, and linear deployments  |  Weighted aliases for gradual deployments  |

cells.col2: Native blue/green, canary, and linear deployments
cells.col3: Weighted aliases for gradual deployments

rows.text: |  Pricing model  |  Per second billing for vCPU and memory used; Fargate Spot available for x86 and ARM  |  Per invocation and duration (GB-seconds); Lambda Managed Instances offer EC2-based pricing  |

cells.col2: Per second billing for vCPU and memory used; Fargate Spot available for x86 and ARM
cells.col3: Per invocation and duration (GB-seconds); Lambda Managed Instances offer EC2-based pricing

rows.text: |  Concurrency limits  |  Based on cluster capacity  |  1000 concurrent executions by default (can be increased)  |

cells.col3: 1000 concurrent executions by default (can be increased)

rows.text: |  Event-driven invocation  |  Requires additional setup  |  Native support for various AWS event sources  |

cells.col3: Native support for various AWS event sources

rows.text: |  Cold start mitigation  |  Lazy loading images with Seekable OCI (SOCI) can speed up starting Fargate tasks  |  Provisioned concurrency, SnapStart (for Java, Python, and .NET), and Lambda Managed Instances available  |

cells.col2: Lazy loading images with Seekable OCI (SOCI) can speed up starting Fargate tasks
cells.col3: Provisioned concurrency, SnapStart (for Java, Python, and .NET), and Lambda Managed Instances available

rows.text: |  Package size limit  |  No specific limit (container size limited by configured ephemeral storage, 200 GiB maximum)  |  250 MB unzipped, including layers, 10 GB for container image deployments  |

cells.col2: No specific limit (container size limited by configured ephemeral storage, 200 GiB maximum)
cells.col3: 250 MB unzipped, including layers, 10 GB for container image deployments
